detail: Reconciled after the fact: the actual SELL_TO_CLOSE order (client_order_id 461d4b80a1d74915a2ffe9582b3dbab8) filled for real at 2026-10-19T17:09:04.719Z, confirmed directly against the broker's order record -- the live session crashed immediately afterward on an unrelated, unguarded re-check (see CLAUDE.md and the same-day main.ts fix), which is why exit_filled was never logged by the running process itself. Broker confirmed flat (no SPY position, no open orders) at the time of this reconciliation. realizedPnl excludes ~$0.11 in regulatory/clearing/SEC fees across both legs (new to live trading -- the paper account never charged any).

Reconciled by hand: the running process's own exit_filled for this trade was never logged (the job's git push failed on a rebase conflict against an unrelated same-minute commit, so the whole commit -- including today's entry_filled -- never reached origin; reconstructed here from the Actions build log plus the broker's own order record for client_order_id 3585a6a7f097473faa89feb839a5fdb5, filled_price 0.84). This number is the TRUE isolated P&L for this agent's own position only -- it excludes the unrelated SPY 770-strike sale recorded separately below, which the running process's exitPrice/realizedPnl had WRONGLY averaged into a single blended number (previously would have shown exitPrice 1.02/realizedPnl -93 -- do not use those; they were never actually correct for either position).

The user had separately, manually bought a SPY 770-strike call in this same shared Individual Margin account. This agent's exitPosition() retry loop found it via findHeldCall()'s old unfiltered 'any SPY call expiring today' logic, mistook it for its own position (actual entry was the 771 strike), and sold it for real: client_order_id 9b3c29eff3de409ab35cba65d5a88028, filled_price 1.21, filled_quantity 1, 2026-10-20T15:12:35.052Z -- confirmed directly against the broker's order record. The user confirmed they bought it and, by coincidence, were glad it got sold given a market move that day; this was not the agent 'helping' by design, just luck -- the bug is real and was fixed the same day (findHeldCall() now requires an exact strike match; see CLAUDE.md and the same-day main.ts commit). Cost basis for the user's own purchase was not found in this account's recent order history (no matching BUY order for a 770 strike appears in the last ~13 entries returned by /openapi/trade/order/history), so the true gain/loss to the user from the $1.21 sale is not independently confirmed here.
